evidence.description: The HUD helper selects the highest residential-ratio row per ZIP and full-joins workbooks; the DOL helper reads from row 11 and renames the ZIP field.
evidence.quote:
get_hud_data <- function(.paths) {
  lst_hud <- purrr::map(
    .x = .paths,
    .f = ~ openxlsx::read.xlsx(.x) %>%
      tibble::as_tibble() %>%
      janitor::clean_names() %>%
      dplyr::group_by(zip) %>%
      dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(res_ratio)) %>%
      dplyr::slice(1) %>%
      dplyr::ungroup() %>%
      dplyr::select(-c(res_ratio:tot_ratio)),
    .progress = TRUE
  )

  tab_hud <- purrr::reduce(lst_hud, full_join, by = "zip")
  names(tab_hud) <- c(names(tab_hud)[1], paste0(names(tab_hud)[-1], "_hud"))
  return(tab_hud)
}

get_dol_data <- function(.paths) {
  tab_dol <- openxlsx::read.xlsx(.paths, startRow = 11) %>%
    janitor::clean_names() %>%
    dplyr::rename(zip = zip_code) %>%
    dplyr::select(-state, -x9)
  names(tab_dol) <- c(names(tab_dol)[1], paste0(names(tab_dol)[-1], "_dol"))
  return(tab_dol)

evidence.description: The helper normalizes first and middle names and derives lookup years from issue dates, 50 and 30 years earlier.
evidence.quote:
gender_prepare_name_table <- function(.tab) {
  .tab %>%
    dtplyr::lazy_dt() %>%
    dplyr::select(ind_id, first_name, middle_name, issue_date) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(ind_id, issue_date) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(ind_id) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(issue_date = dplyr::first(issue_date)) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::distinct() %>%
    tibble::as_tibble() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      first_name = first_name %>%
        gsub("[[:punct:]]", " ", .) %>%
        gsub("([[:space:]]|[[:blank:]])+", " ", .) %>%
        trimws(.) %>%
        stringr::str_to_title(.),
      middle_name = middle_name %>%
        gsub("[[:punct:]]", " ", .) %>%
        gsub("([[:space:]]|[[:blank:]])+", " ", .) %>%
        trimws(.) %>%
        stringr::str_to_title(.),
      dplyr::across(c(first_name, middle_name), ~ dplyr::if_else(nchar(.) < 2, NA_character_, .))
    ) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(c(first_name, middle_name), names_to = "name_type", values_to = "name") %>%
    dtplyr::lazy_dt() %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(name)) %>%
    dplyr::distinct(ind_id, issue_date, name) %>%
    tibble::as_tibble() %>%
    tidytext::unnest_tokens(name, name, to_lower = FALSE) %>%
    dtplyr::lazy_dt() %>%
    dplyr::filter(nchar(name) > 1) %>%
    dplyr::distinct() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      year_min = lubridate::year(issue_date) - 50,
      year_max = lubridate::year(issue_date) - 30
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(-issue_date) %>%
    tibble::as_tibble()
}

race_get_table_by_method <- function(.lst_race, .tab_ind_race, .path_race_census, .path_race_floter) {
  tmp <- dtplyr::lazy_dt(dplyr::select(.tab_ind_race, ind_id, state, surname, age, sex, county))

    dplyr::select(
      ind_id, race,
      prediction = probability, guess_diff = guessdiff,
      method = predictionmethod
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(race = tolower(race))
  
  tab_race_floter <- rio::import(.path_race_floter) %>%
    dplyr::select(
      ind_id, race,
      prediction = probability, guess_diff = guessdiff,

evidence.description: The datasheet identifies the CPA license source as NASBA/state boards and states the collection period for the paper data.
evidence.quote:
We collect CPA license data from the National Association of State Boards of Accountancy
(NASBA) public centralized repository of CPA license data, which compiles publicly available
CPA license data from individual State Boards of Accountancy websites. Masters program
graduation data is publicly available from the Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System
(IPEDS). CPA exam data is publicly available from the National Association of State Boards
of Accountancy (NASBA). Financial aid data is publicly available from IPEDS and the
National Center of Science and Engineering Statistics. Historical job postings data is publicly
available from the github for “The Evolution of Work in the United States” and “New
Technologies and the Labor Market.” We collected these data between January 2021 and
March 2021.
